name: Palestinian nationalism
summary: Palestinian nationalism is the national movement of the Palestinian Arabs for self-determination and sovereignty in Palestine. It holds that Palestinians are one people with an inherent identity and a right of return, that the loss of 1948 and the occupation of 1967 are illegitimate, and that they are owed a state with Jerusalem as capital. The mainstream, the PLO and Fatah, moved from armed struggle for all of Mandatory Palestine to a state on the 1967 territories alongside Israel; its Islamist wing, Hamas, keeps armed resistance and rejects recognition.
scope: The national question only: the Palestinian people, its territory, return, sovereignty, Jerusalem, relations with Zionism and the Arab nation, and the means accepted. Taken from the PLO's Covenant of 1968, the 1974 programme, Arafat's 1974 UN speech, Fatah's constitution, the 1988 Declaration of Independence and National Council communique, and the 1993 letters of recognition, with Hamas's 2017 Document of General Principles as the Islamist strand where it differs. Where the PLO texts differ across time the 1988-1993 position is the committed adherent's present view. The economy, welfare, social policy and the wider programme of Fatah, the PLO or the Palestinian Authority are not counted unless the national texts state them.

missingStatements.text: A people living under foreign military occupation has the right to resist it by armed force.
missingStatements.rationale: The Covenant and Fatah make armed struggle the way to liberation, the 1988 National Council renews the right of peoples to resist occupation, and Arafat calls such confrontation legitimate and just.

missingStatements.text: Settlements built by an occupying power in occupied territory should be removed.
missingStatements.rationale: The 1988 National Council demands annulment of annexation measures and removal of the settlements Israel established since 1967.

missingStatements.text: A state may be proclaimed on part of a people's claimed homeland if it renounces force and accepts the existing neighbouring state.
missingStatements.rationale: The 1988 Declaration proclaims a state on Palestinian territory and rejects force, and the 1993 letters recognise Israel's right to exist in peace, while Hamas and the Covenant reject partition.

notes: Searched the Covenant, the 1974 programme and Arafat speech, Fatah's constitution, the 1988 declaration and communique, the 1993 letters and Hamas's 2017 document theme by theme. Government, economy, society, ecology and technology are almost silent because the national texts are about the national question; the Declaration's equal rights, parliamentary democracy and non-discrimination clauses are the only stated positions there. The 1968 Covenant took positions on Israel's legitimacy that the PLO declared inoperative in 1993; the text of the 1996 amendment was not opened, so which articles remain is not settled here. Hamas and the PLO split on recognition, borders and means. Review (2026-10-30): distinct-gender-roles nulled (equal public rights is a narrower case). PNC texts are treated as the national movement's common ground across its factions; Hamas is the separate strand. Deepen pass (2026-10-30): read the PNC political statements of 1977, 1981, 1983, 1984 and 1987, Fatah's 2009 programme, the 1964 Covenant, the 1988 Hamas Covenant, Arafat's 1988 Geneva speech, the 1996 amendment and Arafat's 1998 list of nullified articles (Covenant arts. 6-10, 15, 19-23 and 30 nullified; parts of 1-5, 11-14, 16-18, 25-27, 29 too), and two scholarly surveys of the PNC resolutions. Themes searched: government, culture, society, means, world, economy; the PNC texts and programmes are about the national question and repeat the same positions session after session, so they added few new answers (the Declaration's rule of law, independent judiciary, parliamentary democracy and freedom of expression). The 1964 Basic Law, the 1965-1974 and 1991-1993 session texts, the PFLP's 2000 programme and the DFLP's 1975 programme were opened or found but are Marxist programmes on class and economy or lack full open text, and no answer rests on them; Fatah's 2009 Internal Charter is organisational. Not found as open full text: the 1964 PLO Basic Law, the 1984-1987 session political programmes beyond the statements, Fatah's 2009 Five Points. Answers resting only on nullified Covenant articles were nulled (patriotic-education) or re-sourced. Review (2026-10-30, after the deepen pass): party-controls-media nulled (freedom of expression does not settle it).
